debt_events.summary: Final settlement of the convertible-debt exchange: 97.44% of the previously outstanding 2027 notes were exchanged. In total, the company issued $209.721 million of second-lien 2030 notes, including the steering-committee premium, and 317,834,446 common shares; $29.459 million of 2027 notes remained. This was a major debt restructuring with creditor concessions and substantial shareholder dilution; no agency default classification was verified.

Company reported covenant compliance under its 2030 notes. Those notes have a $15 million quarterly minimum-liquidity covenant, mature on 2030-10-15 and carry 7% interest, or 9.5% when paid in kind; the delayed-draw facility was fully drawn. These are reported compliance facts, not evidence of a current payment default.

Executed second supplemental indenture removing certain restrictions on repurchasing or exchanging 2027 notes for cash and/or equity, and extending the conversion interest make-whole period to 2029-01-15. This was covenant flexibility, not a disclosed breach.

Entered privately negotiated agreements to exchange approximately $15 million principal of 2027 notes for common stock at 96% of face value. Initial issuance was to be 1,097,444 shares, with up to 848,265 additional shares at final settlement scheduled around September 28, subject to closing conditions; the opened filing does not confirm completion.

output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-10-21, credit and counterparty risk is high: persistent operating losses and cash consumption, a major 2025 debt restructuring and constrained equity-market access weaken the capacity to honour longer-term obligations ([June 2026 10-Q](https://investors.beyondmeat.com/static-files/3b3bf43f-d7e6-4aa2-aa01-c694cfa84502)). Unrestricted cash of $171.369 million at June 27, reported covenant compliance and management’s conditional twelve-month liquidity assessment provide a near-term buffer, while the September agreement to exchange approximately $15 million of 2027 notes for equity would reduce refinancing pressure if completed ([September exchange filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655210/000119312526398531/d186483d8k.htm)). Historical disputed supplier-payment reports and the $38.9 million litigation accrual warrant caution with unsecured exposure, but do not establish a current missed payment or insolvency ([Food Dive](https://www.fooddive.com/news/beyond-meats-financial-woes-magnified-through-late-payments/724812/); [10-Q](https://investors.beyondmeat.com/static-files/3b3bf43f-d7e6-4aa2-aa01-c694cfa84502)).

distress_signals.summary: Management stated in the June 27 10-Q that existing cash and anticipated operating cash flows should fund operations and foreseeable cash requirements for the next twelve months, conditional on revenue, cash-flow and cost assumptions. It also disclosed inability to access its ATM equity program because it no longer satisfied Form S-3 eligibility; this limits financing flexibility. No formal going-concern warning was identified in this 10-Q.

Quarterly revenue declined 8.2% year over year, operating loss was $30.806 million and adjusted EBITDA remained negative. Reported net income was driven primarily by a $57.7 million non-cash debt-extinguishment gain, rather than profitable operations.

The 10-Q continued to disclose existing material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting and corrections to comparative-period accounting. It also reported continuing charges from cessation of China operations in 2025 and partial headquarters lease termination.

Leadership transition: on September 30, Mr. Krishnaswamy began full-time employment and replaced interim COO David Boken; Boken was also to step down as interim Chief Transformation Officer effective October 7, with duties reassigned. This is operational restructuring, not evidence of a CFO departure.

payment_behaviour.summary: Historical, disputed trade-payment report: Food Dive cited Creditsafe data that 36% of 2024 bills were at least 91 days overdue. Beyond Meat called the figures highly inaccurate and vehemently disputed the characterization. This is not a verified current delinquency rate or proof of a particular unpaid invoice.

Sonate trademark litigation: jury awarded $23.5 million actual damages and $15.4 million disgorgement; Beyond Meat recorded a $38.9 million litigation accrual. As reported in the June 2026 10-Q, post-trial motions remained pending. This is contingent litigation exposure, not a supplier collection judgment or established payment default.

Former co-manufacturer dispute settled in Beyond Meat’s favour: the 10-Q reports $4 million received in June and the remaining $7.1 million including interest received on July 10 under an $11 million settlement. This dispute does not establish unpaid supplier obligations by Beyond Meat.
